Use a good epoxy, maybe mix it off ratio, do some surface prep before you try gluing, and post cure it at high temp if at all possible.

A - find an epoxy that you're confident will hold to stone. JB Weld is not bad, but you should know that much of their product is just filler to cut down the cost per gallon. Use whatever your budget allows and definitely look into compounds made for stone bonding.

B - epoxy is fairly tolerant to bring mixed off its ratio. If you mix a little extra of the epoxy with a little less of the hardener, you'll end up with a softer overall product that has more flex. Since stone has no flex of any kind, this would make it a little more durable. (Think about how super glue would just break, we want the opposite of that) THIS STEP IS DANGEROUS and you can skip it if you feel unsure! Most I would ever mix off ratio is maybe 5-10% so unless you have accurate hands you might not even want to worry.

C - prep your surface! Rough it up with a fine sandpaper and then wash the bonding surface really well with rubbing alcohol. Maybe not acetone, just in case there's a sealant on the stone surface.

D - epoxy will get thinner as it warms up, but it also cures faster. Warm up your stone pieces to maybe 90°F before application of the epoxy and you'll get better penetration into the pores of the stone, but watch for leakage. Once the epoxy is hard, it's still only maybe 70% cured. At room temp, best it might ever achieve is 85%. Put it in the oven for a few hours at 90°F and you can be much more confident that it's fully cured.
